stories.title: Update: Jamia reports conflict on when offline classes resume; latest says Tuesday 10 November, with mid-term exams offline from 16 to 21 November
stories.body: IANS reported on Friday 30 October that Jamia Millia Islamia will keep online classes until Monday 9 November and resume offline classes from Tuesday 10 November, quoting the order as saying offline classes shall be conducted from that date. It also said the second mid-term exams, earlier planned online, will be held offline from Monday 16 to Saturday 21 November, and other student activities move offline under the 2026-27 calendar. This differs from an office order dated Wednesday 28 October, reported by PTI and Outlook India, that kept classes online until Tuesday 24 November with online end-semester exams, and from The Wire's report of Monday 2 November.
stories.check: NEEDS CHECK: three dates are in circulation for offline classes (2 Nov, 10 Nov, and online until 24 Nov). The 10 November report is the latest and quotes an order, but the order itself was not seen and no Jamia press release carries it. Confirm the current notice with Jamia before publishing.

sources.label: PTI via Siasat Daily (28 Oct order: online until 24 Nov)

stories.title: Update: Delhi Police register FIR against unknown persons over Jamia vandalism; university alleges damage to gates and CCTV on night of 27 October
stories.body: Delhi Police registered an FIR on Thursday 29 October against unknown persons at Jamia Nagar police station over alleged vandalism at Jamia Millia Islamia, on a complaint from the university administration, IANS and the Pioneer reported, citing police officials. A Jamia press release dated Wednesday 28 October says protesting students and local residents damaged gates and boundary walls, brought down Gate No. 4C and damaged the CCTV control room and cameras on the night of Tuesday 27 October. It also says masked protesters went to the boys' hostels and that women faculty and wardens were threatened. No arrests were reported in these accounts.
stories.check: The damage and threat claims are the university's and were not independently confirmed; protesters' response was not found. The release does not mention police or an FIR, and the police statement is from unnamed officials. The release PDF was read, but the release page carries no printed date (28 Oct is from the file name and the PDF). Confirm with Delhi Police and Jamia.

stories.title: Jamia staff hold thanksgiving programme after union-poll order, demand action over graffiti and vandalism
stories.body: A Jamia Millia Islamia press release dated Friday 30 October says more than 2,000 teaching and non-teaching staff gathered at 3.30 pm on the Ansari Auditorium lawns to thank the administration for resolving the students' union dispute through the order of Thursday 29 October. The release credits the administration with ending what it calls a 20-year deadlock and thanks the Ministries of Education and Home Affairs. It says staff demanded strict action against those responsible for anti-national graffiti, slogans and vandalism of walls, gates and infrastructure, and criticised social media framing of the outcome as a win for one side.
stories.check: Single source and the account is the university's, issued by its public relations office. The release does not state the order's terms. Students' response was not found. The release page carries no printed date (30 Oct is from the file name). Confirm with Jamia.
